pillar_reactions.evidence: Checked the structure back before agreeing: 'and so the three to four times a week, it's going to be mobility and the workout?' then confirmed the daily mobility routine sat on top. Practical rather than enthusiastic.

Asked how it would actually work before responding to it: 'So how do you guys do that? Do you want me to keep a food diary or how does that work?' He had already volunteered that he intermittent fasts noon to eight and needs protein tips, so the pillar largely restated his own practice.

Probed the mechanism — 'And log into an app?' — and accepted the answer with 'Check. Check.' He had already named accountability as the thing he most needs, so this pillar was aligned with his own diagnosis and drew no pushback.

anchors.raw: Yeah, no, the other programs I've seen were a little less.
anchors.competitor: Unnamed competing online kettlebell coaches, including one he identified only by Instagram handle
anchors.note: He has a live competitive process running with calls booked the following week. The anchor is soft — 'a little less' — which means it was addressable, and the rep answered it by conceding premium position rather than by quantifying the difference.

anchors.raw: I mean, if we could do something in the 2 grand range, then I think we could, I think 4 grand is a little bit out of my budget, I'll be honest.
anchors.note: A stated ceiling of $2,000 against a $4,000 three-month quote. Roughly $667 a month, which sits inside the band he later says competitors occupy — so the gap is smaller than it appears and was never tested.

anchors.raw: if I do a bunch of others, and everybody's coming around the same price range, then yeah, then it goes from seven and a half to nine, right? But I've got to do my due diligence and see what else is out there.
anchors.note: He stated the exact condition under which he buys — market confirmation that the price is normal. The rep had that evidence available from other calls in this period, where competing coaching programmes were quoted at $600 to $1,000 a month, and supplied none of it.

unmet_demand.want: A three-month term rather than six
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The stated offer runs six and twelve months. He raised the three-month requirement in his opening answer and repeated it, and the rep priced one at $4,000 rather than pointing to an existing tier.

unmet_demand.want: Programming that flexes between a 30-minute and a 60-minute session depending on what time he wakes
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He described the need precisely — 'it would be nice to get a program and be like, okay, if you've got an hour, do this, if you've got 30 minutes, do this' — and the rep answered 'So you can sort of decide in there' without confirming that alternates are actually programmed.

unmet_demand.want: Conditioning benchmarks and testing, including VO2, plus progressions that do not leave him wiped out at round five
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked directly — 'I don't know if you guys can do tests, like to test my VO2' — and the question was never answered anywhere on the call.
